title: How Poland’s Restrictive Tax Treatment of Losses Penalizes Risk-Taking and Business Expansion
summary: Poland has one of the most restrictive approaches to the tax treatment of losses in the OECD. Loss carryover provisions allow businesses to deduct their losses in one year against taxable income in another, smoothing their taxable income over time. Their absence or restriction leads to firms with more variable profits and losses over time being taxed at higher rates, penalizing risky investment, such as research and development (R&D), and business expansion.
ai_summary: Poland's restrictive tax treatment of loss carryovers, one of the most stringent in the OECD, penalizes risky investments like R&D and business expansion. This policy leads to firms with variable profits and losses being taxed at higher effective rates.
